chunks: From him, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Basir, who said:
A man does not have the status of being married (muhsan) until there is a woman with him whose door he can lock upon her.

key_terms.مُحْصَن: Muhsan — the legal status of being married/chaste; a person who has had lawful marital intercourse. From the root h-s-n meaning fortress/protection, as marriage is seen as a protection of chastity.
key_terms.يُغْلِقُ عَلَيْهَا بَابَهُ: He locks his door upon her — a legal formula indicating full marital cohabitation and conjugal access, the minimum condition for ihsan.

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a man to be considered muhsan (married) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the legal condition for a man to be considered 'muhsan' (married/chaste) in Islamic jurisprudence. The condition is that he must have a wife with whom he cohabits and has marital access — symbolized by the ability to lock the door upon her. This ruling is significant because the status of ihsan (being married) affects the severity of legal penalties for adultery (hadd al-zina) in classical Islamic law: a muhsan person who commits zina is subject to stoning (rajm), while an unmarried person is subject to flogging.
